note: Doc 13 Part One, verbatim. Used when an object has no written response and no object-specific override. Pools ROTATE and never repeat consecutively. Doc 06: an unhandled combination gets a Thad line, never a generic refusal -- the pool is itself comedy.

PICK_UP: I have tried. It has views.
That is not mine, and more to the point it will not come.
No. It is part of the town.
USE: I have no plan for it.
I should want something first. I have not got a want to hand.
OPEN: It does not open. Very little here does.
There is no way into it.
It is not that kind of thing.
CLOSE: It is already as closed as it intends to be.
PUSH: It does not move. I have committed to this now and it still does not move.
PULL: It stays where it is, and I look like a man pulling at a thing.
TALK_TO: It has said nothing and I have said nothing and we are both content.
I would like it on record that I considered it.

people.note: Doc 07: verbs other than TALK TO, pointed at a person. Thad's lines, not the character's, and shared across everyone -- 'I am not going to push a stranger' is the same sentiment whichever stranger it is. Before these existed, every verb on an ambient character opened their dialogue tree, so PUSH started a conversation.
LOOK_AT: A person. I have decided to be polite about it.
PICK_UP: No. I have thought about it for exactly as long as it deserves.
PUSH: I have never pushed anybody. I am not starting on a street this muddy.
PULL: Pulling a stranger is how a man ends up known for something.
OPEN: They are already as open as they intend to be.
CLOSE: One does not close a person. One is closed by them, usually at cards.
USE: I would not know where to begin, and the beginning is the part people object to.
LISTEN_TO: Breathing, and the particular silence of somebody deciding whether I am worth their afternoon.
